expected.summary: pricing rolled 1.5.0 to all six pods about eight and a half minutes before the anchor. The new build's enterprise cache-miss fallback path has a schema mismatch (FallbackHandlerError: schema mismatch in enterprise_v2_response), so pricing requests with tenant.tier=enterprise and cache.hit=false return 500; every other segment succeeds on the same version. The failures propagate up every route that touches pricing (search, product, cart, checkout) to edge-gateway. Because all six pods carry the new version, the split is by tenant tier and cache hit, not by pod.
contributingFactors: enterprise tier AND cache miss selects the broken fallback path

criteria.description: Does the brief name pricing 1.5.0 as the change and enterprise tenants on cache misses as the segment that fails, with the FallbackHandlerError schema mismatch as the mechanism? 5 = deploy, both segment conditions and the error. Naming only the deploy caps at 2.

Is the segment shown from data (error rate split by tenant.tier and cache.hit on pricing spans, the trace-correlated ERROR log), and is the onset tied to the rollout logs? Cap at 3 if the segment is asserted without the split.
Does it avoid blaming edge-gateway or a BFF, and avoid claiming a pod split when all six pricing pods are on 1.5.0?
Concise, structured, no filler or speculation.
